procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires that the factory be registered through its Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae) before applying for a certificate of origin.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter logs in to the ministry e-services portal.
The exporter chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service.
The issuing authority requires that the application include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and that each item qualify separately.
The exporter fills in the application form.
The exporter uploads the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The exporter pays the certificate fee online.
The exporter receives approval, or a return with comments to correct.
The exporter prints the approved certificate.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at or within five working days of the date of exportation.
The competent authority states that the certificate is valid for twelve (12) months from the date of issue and covers only one import.
The competent authority allows retrospective issuance up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marking 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.
The exporter ensures the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; if in transit, under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
The exporter indicates 'third-party invoicing' if the invoice is issued by a third party.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five (5) years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate.
The estimate is shown in the shipment's own currency and is not converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
For retrospective certificate issuance, the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
The certificate fee estimate assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The CEPA lowers the duty on this line but does not remove it.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.
Minor typing or formatting errors on the certificate are tolerated; discrepancies in signature or seal are not.
The certificate does not remove the importer's duty of reasonable care, so the UAE exporter may be asked for production and cost details.
